chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I heard him saying: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: I do not apply the hadd of cutting (for theft) regarding open Daghara, and it is Khalsah, but I reprimand him.'

key_terms.أَقْطَعُ: Aqtu': I cut (referring to the hadd punishment of amputating the hand for theft).
key_terms.أُعَزِّرُهُ: U'azziruhu: I reprimand him / apply ta'zir (discretionary punishment).
key_terms.الدَّغَارَةِ: Daghara: Picking up lost property or belongings of another person.
key_terms.الْخَلْسَةُ: Al-Khalsah: Stealthily taking or snatching something; here used to define the nature of Daghara.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Daghara and theft regarding the hadd of cutting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguished between open theft and 'Daghara' (piding up lost property), ruling that the fixed hadd of hand amputation does not apply to the latter because it lacks the element of stealth (khalsah). Instead, the perpetrator is subject to ta'zir, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that hadd penalties require strict adherence to their specific conditions, allowing for judicial discretion in cases of ambiguity.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Iasws do not cut regarding Al-Dagara (picking up somebody else’s belongings) openly and it is stealth, but Iasws reprimand him’.
